provenance.Annotator model/name: Copilot SDK AI assistant (subagent; model version not exposed)
provenance.Collection method: AI-assisted cause annotation via Copilot SDK in VS Code; not human annotation.
provenance.Inter-annotator agreement: Not measured; single annotator, no adjudication.
provenance.Evidence shown: cases.json only: dev query text and metadata, source title/abstract, D50 top-20 titles/abstracts, completed top-20 grades with label provenance and judge reasons, stage ranks and graded-loss attribution.
Cautions: Causes are an AI assistant's reading of titles and abstracts, not validated ground truth.
Grades are LLM judgments (GPT-5.4 mini, GPT-6 ASTRA reference, GPT-6 Terra completion), not human labels.
No relevance labels, rankings or other evidence were created or changed.

codebook.status: codebook-v0 was written before any case evidence was read. codebook-v1 was refined after reading cases.json for all 16 cases and before assigning any annotation; changes are listed below and the v0 causes were not removed.

changes.reason: Six of the ten lowest-nDCG cases have the source at D50 rank 1 as the only grade-2 paper; their loss comes from ordering partial matches, which no v0 code describes without calling it a system error.

changes.change: vocabulary_gap may apply to other relevant papers, not only the source.
changes.reason: In lowest-nDCG cases with the source found, paraphrased wording can still pull off-target papers into ranks 2-10.

changes.change: label_gap split into a primary rule (wrong grade 2 or clearly wrong grade 0) and a secondary-only rule (0-vs-1 inconsistency).
changes.reason: Partial-credit disagreements are common in the pool and would otherwise make label_gap the primary cause of every single-target case.

changes.change: Added the selection-reason rule and a primary-cause precedence order.
changes.reason: Several codes can fit one case; a fixed order makes the single annotator's choices reproducible from the rules.

rules: Assign exactly one primary cause: the most specific explanation supported by the shown titles and abstracts.
Use secondary causes only for additional explanations that are also supported by the evidence.
Stage (where the paper was lost) is computed by code, not annotated; mechanism causes are used only when no content-level cause is evident.
The primary cause must explain why the case was selected: for a source miss, why the source is outside the D50 top 10; for a lowest-nDCG case, where the graded loss comes from.

When several causes meet their decision rules, choose the primary in this order: query_generation_artifact, label_gap, competing_near_duplicate, acronym_or_rare_term, vocabulary_gap, single_target_partial_credit, broad_or_underspecified_query, rerank_demotion, stage1_miss.

causes.definition: The query describes the source's contribution in different words from its title and abstract (paraphrase or terminology mismatch).
causes.decision_rule: The source or other relevant papers satisfy the query, but their key concepts appear under different terms, and higher-ranked papers share the query's surface words rather than the specific contribution asked for.

causes.definition: The query hinges on an acronym, named method, dataset or rare term that retrieval or reranking fails to match or resolve.
causes.decision_rule: Removing or expanding one specific rare token would plausibly change the outcome, and that token is in the source but rare or ambiguous in the corpus.

causes.definition: Many papers fit the query about as well as the source; the source is not uniquely best, so the miss is more a measurement limit than a system error.
causes.decision_rule: Several top-10 papers satisfy every stated requirement of the query, and the query omits the details that distinguish the source.

causes.definition: A top-ranked paper addresses nearly the same specific problem and method as the source, displacing it.
causes.decision_rule: At least one top-10 paper matches the source's specific problem and approach, not just its general topic.

causes.definition: The generated query does not describe the source well: it emphasizes details absent from, peripheral to or inconsistent with the source abstract.
causes.decision_rule: A reader of the source title and abstract alone would not judge the source a strong answer to the query.

causes.definition: Relevance labels understate or distort quality: relevant-looking top-10 papers are graded 0 or are unjudged, or grades are inconsistent with the abstracts.
causes.decision_rule: As primary: a grade 2 on a paper that shares only a word or a different sense of a query term, or a grade 0 on a top-10 paper that satisfies all of the query's main constraints, and these grades account for much of the loss. Inconsistent 0-vs-1 grades among partial matches are recorded only as a secondary label_gap.

causes.definition: The query has one clear target (the source), which D50 ranks first or second; few or no other papers meet all its constraints, so the loss comes from how partial matches (grade 0 vs 1) are ordered below it, a metric and label-pool effect more than a user-visible failure.
causes.decision_rule: Source at D50 rank 1 or 2 with grade 2, no grade-2 paper outside the D50 top 10, and the papers below the source each meet only part of the query.

causes.definition: Residual mechanism code: the source or most missing relevant papers never reached the Decision 36 top 50, and no content-level cause is evident.
causes.decision_rule: Use only when the computed stage is Stage 1 and none of the content-level causes above is supported.

causes.definition: Residual mechanism code: the reranker had the source or better-graded papers in its pool but ranked less relevant papers above them.
causes.decision_rule: Use only when the loss is within the reranked pool, the displaced papers are clearly more relevant, and no content-level cause is evident.
